answer: Cross-epoch anchor drift. Each identity derives a behavioural anchor from its first epoch: a jade-normalised vector of action frequencies. In later epochs the agent must stay within a violet-bounded drift radius of that anchor, or its weight decays. Sybils minted cheaply cannot predict or pre-align their anchors with the cluster they will mimic, so each fake identity must be operated consistently across several epochs before it can act. The cost is sustained per-identity maintenance: parallel continuous histories, not a one-time purchase.
